I am a Postdoctoral Associate at the University of Florida's [Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences](https://ifas.ufl.edu/about-us/).
I am an applied economist.
I study how trade, regulation, and environmental change shape firm behavior and market outcomes in food and natural resource industries.
My research connects international trade and agricultural policy with producer adaptation, seafood supply chains, and the economic resilience of coastal communities.
It generates evidence for industry and public decision-makers.

**Contact.** [aceballos@ufl.edu](mailto:aceballos@ufl.edu) · [linkedin.com/in/AdamsCeballos](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adams-ceballos-concha-0403633a/) · PO Box 110240, McCarty B 2120, Gainesville, FL 32611-0240

## Experience

**Jan 2025 – Present** · Postdoctoral Associate · University of Florida, School of Forest, Fisheries & Geomatics Sciences, Gainesville, FL

- Supervised by Savanna Barry and Edward V. Camp on the NOAA RESTORE Act Science Program project [*Seagrass Conservation on Florida's Nature Coast*](https://restoreactscienceprogram.noaa.gov/projects/seagrass-conservation-on-floridas-nature-coast).
- Work with seagrass ecologists, spatial analysts, and environmental lawyers to evaluate pole-and-troll zones that protect propeller-scarred seagrass beds.
- Co-designed the boater survey, hired and trained the field staff, and ran the intercept and email fieldwork. Collected more than 1,000 baseline surveys in Pasco County ahead of new protection zones.
- Estimate boater demand models, including contingent-behavior scenarios, that combine survey, ecological, and administrative data.
- Present findings to resource managers and stakeholders through policy briefs and presentations.

**Jan 2025 – Present** · Researcher, Florida Gulf Fisheries and Seafood Markets · Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) / University of Florida

- Lead the econometric analysis of how fishery regulation, harvesting costs, stock conditions, and seafood markets shape commercial fisher participation. Work with Kotryna Klizentyte, Edward V. Camp, and FWC staff.
- Use harmonized FWC trip-ticket records to study entry and exit, fishing intensity, species switching, dealer relationships, and dockside prices in the stone crab, spiny lobster, pink shrimp, and reef fish fisheries.

**Aug 2021 – Dec 2024** · Graduate Research Assistant · University of Florida, Food & Resource Economics, Gainesville, FL

- Evaluated socioeconomic impacts of harmful algal blooms (2017–2019) on Florida fisheries using fishery-dependent data. Estimated changes in landings and revenues by species and county.
- Built panel datasets of landings, prices, effort, and closures for quasi-experimental analysis. Prepared stakeholder reports.

**Sep 2017 – Jun 2021** · Research Assistant / Project Coordinator · Interdisciplinary Center for Aquaculture Research (INCAR), Concepción, Chile

- Coordinated an interdisciplinary research team that produced the technical basis for the Biobío Region's aquaculture policy. Led working meetings with regional authorities.
- Designed and implemented household and stakeholder surveys. Analyzed socioeconomic outcomes of aquaculture expansion.
- Produced evidence summaries and briefings for public agencies and industry stakeholders. Organized stakeholder workshops.

## Technical skills

- **Causal inference.** Difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, event studies, synthetic control, panel models, welfare analysis, spatial econometrics, and double/debiased machine learning.
- **AI, machine learning, and LLM methods.** Statistical machine learning, LLM agents for studying firm decision-making, factorial experimental design with LLM agents, cross-model evaluation, and high-performance computing (SLURM, UF HiPerGator).
- **Programming.** R (DoubleML, grf, tidyverse, fixest, data.table); Python (EconML, LLM pipelines, pandas, scikit-learn); SQL; Git.
- **Communication.** Executive briefs, reproducible pipelines (Quarto, R Markdown), dashboards (Shiny, Plotly), and maps (QGIS).
- **Domains.** International trade; agricultural, fisheries, and aquaculture economics; natural resource policy and regulation; AI and machine learning methods for applied economics.
- **Languages.** Spanish (native), English (fluent).
